precepts.text: Put out of the camp every leper, every one that hath an issue, and whosoever is defiled by the dead; that is why those men could not come in.
precepts.point: They asked, wherefore are we kept back, that we may not offer an offering of the Lord in his appointed season? And Moses said, stand still, and I will hear what the Lord will command concerning you.

note.label: Numbers 9: The Second Passover and the Cloud over the Tabernacle

precepts.why:
Certain men “were defiled by the dead body of a man, that they could not keep the passover on that day.” The law had already ruled on them: “And the Lord spake unto Moses, saying, Command the children of Israel, that they put out of the camp every leper, and every one that hath an issue, and whosoever is defiled by the dead.”

Whosoever was defiled by the dead was put out of the camp, so those men could not come in with the congregation to make their offering in his appointed season. That is why they asked, “wherefore are we kept back”, and Moses said, “Stand still, and I will hear what the Lord will command concerning you.”

precepts.text: He maketh the clouds his chariot; the cloud over the tabernacle was his chariot.
precepts.point: That cloud is the chariot of the Most High: he maketh the clouds his chariot, and that is what sat over the top of the tabernacle.

note.label: Numbers 9: The Second Passover and the Cloud over the Tabernacle

precepts.why:
On the day the tabernacle was reared up the cloud covered it, “and at even there was upon the tabernacle as it were the appearance of fire, until the morning.” That cloud is the chariot of the Most High: “Who layeth the beams of his chambers in the waters: who maketh the clouds his chariot: who walketh upon the wings of the wind.”

He maketh the clouds his chariot, and that is what sat over the top of the tabernacle, the cloud by day and the appearance of fire by night.

precepts.text: When the cloud was taken up from over the tabernacle, the children of Israel went onward in all their journeys; Numbers revisits what Exodus recorded.
precepts.point: At the commandment of the Lord they rested in the tents, and at the commandment of the Lord they journeyed; they kept the charge of the Lord by the hand of Moses.

note.label: Numbers 9: The Second Passover and the Cloud over the Tabernacle

precepts.why:
“And when the cloud was taken up from the tabernacle, then after that the children of Israel journeyed: and in the place where the cloud abode, there the children of Israel pitched their tents.” Numbers revisits what Exodus recorded: “And when the cloud was taken up from over the tabernacle, the children of Israel went onward in all their journeys.”

Wherever the chariot went, Israel got up and followed it, the same way it led them across the Red Sea. Whether it were two days, or a month, or a year that the cloud tarried, they abode in their tents; and when it was taken up they journeyed, whether by day or by night. That is how they knew where they needed to stay and when to move: at the commandment of the Lord they rested, and at the commandment of the Lord they journeyed, keeping the charge of the Lord by the hand of Moses.

precepts.text: Certain men defiled by the dead body of a man could not keep the passover that day; they asked Moses wherefore they were kept back.
precepts.point: The Most High answered through Moses with a second keeping: the man unclean by reason of a dead body, or far off on a journey, keeps the passover the fourteenth day of the second month at even, eating it with unleavened bread and bitter herbs.
precepts.why:
“He that toucheth the dead body of any man shall be unclean seven days.” There is history on this law. In Numbers 9 “there were certain men, who were defiled by the dead body of a man, that they could not keep the passover on that day.”

They came before Moses and Aaron and said, “We are defiled by the dead body of a man: wherefore are we kept back, that we may not offer an offering of the Lord in his appointed season among the children of Israel?” It was this very statute that kept them back: unclean seven days by a dead body, they could not keep the passover on the appointed day.

precepts.text: The unclean by a dead body or far off on a journey keep the passover the fourteenth day of the second month with unleavened bread and bitter herbs.
precepts.point: The Most High answered through Moses with a second keeping: the man unclean by reason of a dead body, or far off on a journey, keeps the passover the fourteenth day of the second month at even, eating it with unleavened bread and bitter herbs.
precepts.why:
Because a man that touches a dead body is unclean seven days, certain men could not keep the passover on its day, and the Most High answered through Moses with a second keeping.

“If any man of you or of your posterity shall be unclean by reason of a dead body, or be in a journey afar off, yet he shall keep the passover unto the Lord. The fourteenth day of the second month at even they shall keep it, and eat it with unleavened bread and bitter herbs.”

The man unclean by reason of a dead body, or far off on a journey, still keeps the passover, on the fourteenth day of the second month at even, with unleavened bread and bitter herbs. The uncleanness of Numbers 19:11 does not release him from the passover; it moves him to the second month.

precepts.text: A man defiled by a dead body or on a far journey may keep the Passover in the second month, the provision Hezekiah relied on.
precepts.point: They make a proclamation from Beersheba to Dan to come keep the Passover, for they had not done it for a long time in the way it was written.
precepts.why:
In the wilderness “they kept the passover on the fourteenth day of the first month at even”. But “there were certain men, who were defiled by the dead body of a man, that they could not keep the passover on that day”, and they asked, “wherefore are we kept back, that we may not offer an offering of the Lord in his appointed season”?

The Lord answered: “If any man of you or of your posterity shall be unclean by reason of a dead body, or be in a journey afar off, yet he shall keep the passover unto the Lord. The fourteenth day of the second month at even they shall keep it, and eat it with unleavened bread and bitter herbs.” A man defiled or on a far journey may keep the Passover in the second month.

That is the provision Hezekiah relied on. Now that the temple was cleansed, the king and congregation took counsel “to keep the passover in the second month. For they could not keep it at that time, because the priests had not sanctified themselves sufficiently, neither had the people gathered themselves together to Jerusalem.” So he sent letters “to all Israel and Judah”, even “to Ephraim and Manasseh”, with a proclamation “from Beer–sheba even to Dan”, “for they had not done it of a long time in such sort as it was written.”

precepts.text: When the cloud was taken up the children of Israel journeyed, and where the cloud abode there they pitched their tents, teaching us to move only when He moves.
precepts.point: The lesson is that the Most High wants us on one accord, moving when He moves and standing when He stands, just as the powers of heaven do only what He commands.

note.label: Ezekiel 1: The Vision by the River Chebar

precepts.why:
“And when the cloud was taken up from the tabernacle, then after that the children of Israel journeyed: and in the place where the cloud abode, there the children of Israel pitched their tents.”

“When those went, these went; and when those stood, these stood.” The lesson is that the Most High wants us on one accord, moving when He moves and standing when He stands, just as the powers of heaven do only what He commands. Israel pitched their tents where the cloud abode and journeyed only when it was taken up; that is moving only when He moves.

points: The passover carried its rites and its ceremonies: there were things they had to sacrifice and do according to all the ordinances of it, to keep everything in order for the congregation.

points: They asked, wherefore are we kept back, that we may not offer an offering of the Lord in his appointed season? And Moses said, stand still, and I will hear what the Lord will command concerning you.

note.label: Numbers 9: The Second Passover and the Cloud over the Tabernacle

points: The answer came: if any man be unclean by reason of a dead body, or be in a journey afar off, he shall still keep the passover unto the Lord, on the fourteenth day of the second month at even, eating it with unleavened bread and bitter herbs.
Defilement by the dead and traveling afar off were the only two reasons given to miss the appointed day, and even then the passover was kept the following month, not neglected.

The same holds today: many drive trucks and work jobs they cannot get off, and the Most High understands the captivity, but that does not mean you neglect the passover; keep it the second month if it is possible.

note.label: Numbers 9: The Second Passover and the Cloud over the Tabernacle

points: But the man that is clean, and is not in a journey, and forbeareth to keep the passover, shall be cut off from among his people; he brought not the offering of the Lord in his appointed season, and that man shall bear his sin.

This speaks to the one that likes to make excuses. There were no excuses then without being cut off, and there are none now when the holy days come around; if the reason is not according to the bible, it does not stand.

note.label: Numbers 9: The Second Passover and the Cloud over the Tabernacle

points: The stranger that sojourns with Israel and will keep the passover keeps it according to the ordinance of the passover and the manner thereof: one ordinance both for the stranger and for him that was born in the land.

The stranger here is not unbelieving family; it is one of another nation that dwelt among Israel. Even the nations among us had to keep the laws just as we did; they were not getting a pass around us.
